model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between a baseline Mistral-v0.2 model and the same model further fine-tuned on each clinical specialty data, with tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. The horizontal axis represents "Per-specialty terms" and contains six categories labeled Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents "Negative log probability" and ranges from approximately −27 at the bottom to −22 at the top, with tick marks at integer intervals (−27, −26, −25, −24, −23, −22), using an inverted scale where values closer to zero (less negative) appear at the top. For each per-specialty term category, there is a group of seven bars corresponding to different model variants as indicated in the legend: Mistral-v0.2-Base (shown in a dark/black color) and six fine-tuned variants — Cardio (orange), Gastro (yellow/gold), Infect (brown/dark orange), Neuro (light tan/beige), Obstetrics (gray), and Pediatrics (light yellow/cream). Across all six specialty term categories, the Mistral-v0.2-Base bar is consistently the tallest in magnitude (most negative, reaching approximately −26 to −27), indicating the highest negative log-probabilities. The fine-tuned model variants consistently show shorter bars (less negative values, generally ranging from approximately −23 to −25.5), with relatively similar heights among the different fine-tuned versions within each group. The bars within each group are arranged in the same order as listed in the legend, from left to right. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding or outlining, though the base model bar is distinctly darker than the fine-tuned variants, making it easily distinguishable. The grouping pattern is consistent across all six per-specialty term categories, and the relative differences between the base model and fine-tuned variants appear roughly similar across categories, though the absolute values vary by specialty.
